Monoprice VGA to RCA Adapter PC to TV Video Converter- Blue I realize this was a cheap item, manufactured over seas, but after reading many of the reviews, I took a chance anyway. First issue was, like many other reviewers, it was shipped without the USB power cord. I emailed the seller to inform them but as an IT guy, i have tons of these around the house so it wasn't too big of a deal. After getting it all hooked up to an old fashion tube tv, like many others, the screen was black and white, flickering and illegible. i hooked it to a flat screen tv, changed it to NTSC, and was able to see the on screen menu but no picture, only gray bars. I tweaked all the menu options but was never able to see a picture. I made note of the options and reconnected it to my tube TV but after more than 45 minutes trying every combination of options i could, i was never able to get a picture. i've already printed a return label and will send it back tomorrow.

Update: after requesting a return from Amazon and shipping the unit back, I received a response from the seller (keep in mind he did not know that the unit didn't work, only that it did not come with a power cord) His suggestion was to ask Amazon for a refund and order another unit. So let us assume the unit actually did work, He would have wanted me to initiate a return with amazon, print out a label, drop the item off at UPS, spend more money (until i get my refund) to order another unit and cross my fingers that the new one comes with all the pieces. Why not do what any respectable business would do and just send me a power cord?

text_fidelity_a:
Nuforce NE-700X Titanium Coated In-Ear Headphones - Aqua Silver Update after a couple of months

I still love 'em. Everything I put below still holds true. I rarely touch the EQ, and have been able to return to less processing is good processing listening.

One thing to add is that these are the first earbuds I could lay on my side with my head on the pillow and be comfortable. They have minimal strain relief but so far the cords have been perfect. I'd call tangle factor about medium.

++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
Original review

So far I've tried
Skull Candy Titan - For me the best bass sound in this bunch. Tight punchy, accentuated but enjoyably so. Good for working out. But I value accurate bass above all. So I just use these for working out now.
Vsonic GR99 - very nice balanced sounding for $20ish dollars
Vsonic VC02 - Great sounding, but not a lot of bass. But what bass that was there was VERY good. My favorite phones in this list. But I kept losing the ear piece because of the removable wires. After the 2nd time I moved onto the VSD1
Vsonic VSD1 - nice sounding, if somewhat dry. It didn't make me get into my music, and I couldn't get them comfortable in my ears
Brainwaves S1 - These were my least favorite, boomy and not very comfortable, heavy thick wires. The only pair of the above I returned.

What they do well - assume anything not here is more than adequate

Presentation - I feel like I'm getting what the engineer was going for in the mix. More musical than any of the above without falling into a 'warm sound'. A nice mix of forgiving and accurate. Brightness right about where it should be.
Sound Stage - Airy, instruments well placed. Center image is not the strongest, but not lacking. Does a nice job of presenting the room acoustics/reverb in the mix.
Drums - Drums are rendered very well, better than any of the the above.
Cymbals - rendered very well, especially high hat. You can tell the cymbals are made of metal, and not just the tik-tik of the drum stick tip
Treble-sibilance - Close to perfect. Nice and bright without getting into hissy/tizzy. Vocal articulation is good.
Very easy to listen to for long periods of time. They are accurate without being piercing or harsh.
Sounded good right out of the box.

Misc sound notes - distorted electric guitar is just right. They respond to EQ very well, (which the Brainwavz did not do). I really notice when something comes into the mix even if it is soft. And louder things like guitar solos, really punch in the way you hear when mixing in the studio.

If I HAD to critique the sound (this is a review) there is a very-very, (did I mention very?) lack of something in the mids. Think chest/throat area of male vocals. But this is in the realm of sound signature, a matter of taste, not a deficiency and in no way lowers my enjoyment of these.

Build - wires are thin and flexible which is what I wanted. Very nice for wearing over the ear. Microphonics close to none whether worn up or down. No hearing foot steps or wire rubbing/bouncing on clothes. Light cord/cinch is great for running.
Shape - Bullet shaped what can I say, they are light and comfortable. I like the ring of rubber around them. It gives a little grip for inserting/removing them.
I LOVE that they have a red strain relief on the right side. No having to get my glasses to see some tiny R or L printed somewhere. Cord is nice and long, which is nice for using on a treadmill or elliptical trainer, or for wearing the cord under your shirt or down in a pocket.

As much as I liked the over all presentation and frequency response I feel I should point out these are not hella flat-accurate phones (like the VC02). If a true hi-fi sound, bright/accurate/revealing, is what you are after I'd look elsewhere (maybe the VC02) Don't get me wrong, since I used to be a sound engineer, and work on electric guitars, and have very accurate/bright/revealing/fatiguing speakers on my desk, I'm very picky about good accurate sound. But that makes these musical, easy to listen to for very long periods of time and poorly recorded and/or lower quality rips won't be hard to listen to.

The title says it all - the best I've tried yet and the first phones that made me stop 'shopping' for my next pair of phones.

Listening setup. Listening has been through an amp and separate dac connected to my computer playing 192kb - 320k - FLAC music, and through my old Droid Charge (I use this because I can enable the onboard DAC) and my Samsung Note II listening to ripped music (192k or better) or Spotify/Pandora at their highest quality settings available in the premium versions.
text_fidelity_b: Nuforce NE-700X Titanium Coated In-Ear Headphones - Aqua Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) If you're looking for an excellent tablet and e-reader at a great price, look no further. While there are things that it lags with (like playing the Pokemon trading card game, which last I knew, needed to be sideloaded) it does a lot of other things really well. Great experience with watching videos, and reading comics or manga.

If you're into hacking your devices, this tablet (well, the 2015 version that I have) does a really good job of running a clean Nexus rom, which gives you a stock Android experience, and access to the Google play store. I have to say, that was probably the best thing I've done with it so far.

Expandable storage allows you to carry an entire library with you on the go to make sure that you will never run out of things to do. I keep a 128gb micro SD card in mine, but I wouldn't be surprised if you could slot in a larger card, even though it's only officially rated for up to 128gb.

What i'd like to see change for the 2018 version (assuming they do a revamp) would be full 1080p resolution, a snapdragon octacore processor clocked around 2ghz (my free ZTE Blade Zmax has one, and I can't imagine it would be too expensive for them to use it in the fire tablet as well, if even free phones have them now) and 2-3 gb of ram. If Amazon would just do these 3 little upgrades, this tablet would be unbeatable. I wouldn't even mind a mild price bump ($70-80 instead of $50) if these upgrades happened. I would also like to see a future version either running full stock Android OS, or released with the option to unlock the bootloader somehow, to facilitate diy development and cutom roms. But I know that's just asking too much.

If you're looking for a great tablet at an even better price, the Fire 7" is a great choice.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

Logitech G933 Artemis Spectrum – Wireless RGB 7.1 Dolby and DTS Headphone Surround Sound Gaming Headset – PC, PS4, Xbox One, Switch, and Mobile Compatible – Advanced Audio Drivers – Black I got this headset during the 50% off deal and I am really enjoying it with Battlefield 5. I decided to upgrade from my Logitech G430 headset. I was mainly looking for a wireless headset that had great battery life, great sound and did not cost too much. Even without the deal, the $200 price point is still reasonable compared to other wireless headsets. I was considering the Corsair and Astro's before purchasing this one. I am using this headset for my PC only, to game.

The Headset:
- Customizable buttons to change the Equalizer, play/pause, and many other options to choose from
- Convenient volume dial to change sound on the fly. This is great so you dont have to minimize the game and adjust the volume settings with the mouse
- Headset grips my head. I have an angled forehead which my old headset would easily slide off when moving around
- Comfy ear pieces that does not cram my ears and feel uncomfortable
- Comes with long braided charging cable, AUX cables, and RCA cables
- USB adapter to connect the wireless headset it plug and play. You just need to make sure you install the Logitech dashboard to customize the headset
- The Logitech logo and a line down each ear-cuff lights up. To me this is a pointless feature as I am wearing the headset and cannot see the lighting and only uses up battery life. I disabled the lights and my battery life increased by 3 hours.

Sound:
The sound i will say is significantly better than my G430. There are multiple equalizer profiles to choose from (FPS, Cinema, etc.). Once you turn on surround sound and 7.1, it makes a big difference of sounds. You can change the treble, bass, and customize the sound to your liking.

Battery:
I cannot say too much about the battery life, but after a full charge, and turning off the leds on the headset. It said I have 12 hours of battery left. After wearing the headset playing Battlefield 5 for 4 hours, I still had 93% battery life. Overtime with charges and draining, i would assume the life would degrade a bit and would get around 10 hours of battery. I did not check how long it takes to charge the headset from a full depletion.

The only cons I have are the pointless LED lights if you are not showing off your headset. I do feel the headband part of the headset is not as strong as I would have expected it to be, just do not twist headband much.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G933 Artemis Spectrum – Wireless RGB 7.1 Dolby and DTS Headphone Surround Sound Gaming Headset – PC, PS4, Xbox One, Switch, and Mobile Compatible – Advanced Audio Drivers – Black

ARRIS Touchstone TM822G Internet & Voice Modem for XFINITY from Comcast I had a rental modem from Xfinity, saw this one here sold by Amazon Warehouse for cheap, made the leap and got the item in 2 days. Had to wait a few days because the whole family was constantly on the internet. Finally I had a 10-minute window, I worked quickly and disconnected the old one and connected the new one. It powercycled a couple times, while I connected my laptop to the modem via the included ethernet cable. A few minutes in my browser automatically opened up to the xfinity activation page, where it verified I was a legit customer. A few seconds later I was set, and it rebooted the modem.

At this time I hooked up my router to the modem. I tested my wireless speed via speedtest, got 260 Mbps, about double of what I was getting with the old modem. Plus I know in 4 months I'll recoup the cost of the modem by not having to pay Xfinity the monthly rental fee, sweet! All-in-all very easy process to swap out the old unit and the activation was pretty much plug and play. Thanks ARRIS!
text_fidelity_b: ARRIS Touchstone TM822G Internet & Voice Modem for XFINITY from Comcast

D&O LIGHTING LED Video Light Panel – 180W Bi-Color Studio Lighting for Video Recording Filming with 97+ CRI - Aluminum Construction, Big Heat Sink Fins and On-Light V-Mount Adapter Plate for Battery I work in photo/video for a living, and I can tell you that good LEDs aren't cheap. I have worked with hot tungsten lamps for high output and smaller LEDs for lightweight smaller setups, but LED lights that can compete with the output of Tungstens are pricey.
That being said, this is a FANTASTIC light. It has high output yet has the pros of LED panels such as lower power consumption and heat, as well as being dimmable and color adjustable from the panel or remote control. I had the opportunity to use this for a job yesterday setting up an interview in an office setting. My tungsten bulbs would have been too bright and need gels to match the rest of the office. My other smaller LEDs would have cast smaller spots and we all know a larger light source casts a more pleasing glow. It seemed effortless to get the amount of light we needed in a short time.
HOWEVER, I did find that the mounting point was a little bit difficult to use. There are two bolts to secure it to the stand, and both need to be loosened to mount it properly. It took me a few attempts to get it on the stand, one side felt like I was screwing the bolt the wrong direction most of the time. Meanwhile, the light is large and kept wobbling during this overly complicated procedure. It didn't feel like a premium product during that, which I found odd considering the price point. I have lights that cost about half of this one that felt more premium during mounting. But, that being said, once the lights are up it works a treat!
So, a solid 4 stars from me. Almost 5 if the mounting were easier or the price lower to make up for that. But as a light, it does what it should do and well.
text_fidelity_b: D&O LIGHTING LED Video Light Panel – 180W Bi-Color Studio Lighting for Video Recording Filming with 97+ CRI - Aluminum Construction, Big Heat Sink Fins and On-Light V-Mount Adapter Plate for Battery

text_fidelity_a:
Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black For moderate priced earbuds, these are pretty good. The sound quality is much better than average, with smooth response across the range. The highs are detailed, and not shrill. The midbass is clear, with no unnatural peak that sometimes passes for "bass boost". The deep bass is natural, and not artificially strong. Very easy to listen to for extended sessions.

For comfort, these are pretty average -- not the best comfort, but not bad either. There are interchangeable ear tips you can try out for the best fit. There's a lot of personal preference as to what's going to stay in the ear comfortably. The earbuds are angled, so you have to pay attention to the left/right orientation.

This is advertised as "iPhone compatible", meaning that there's a mic with tiny + and - buttons attached to the left ear piece. I'm a BlackBerry guy, and I'm happy to report that the mic works fine with my BlackBerry Bold 9700. But the + and - buttons don't have any effect (they don't raise or lower the volume). However, pressing the small button between the + and - buttons will either pause the song that's playing, or mute a phone call. Pretty handy.

Sound isolation is not a strong point of this set. I wasn't sure what to expect, so I guess I'm not disappointed. Probably you'd want to look elsewhere if sound isolation is important to you.

Durability may also be an issue. The wire is very thin, and it feels fragile, especially where it connects to the earbud. I'll know in 6 to 12 months whether these will stand up to regular use. The 90-degree plug will take wear better for many people, depending on how it connects to your phone, MP3 player or computer. Comes with a little storage pouch, which is good protection for the set when not in use.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black

Amazon Basics Ergonomic Wireless PC Mouse - DPI adjustable - Black I selected this mouse to be a spare for when I am on the go. Amazon-branded things are often of good quality so I was hopeful for this mouse. I came away a bit disappointed due to a couple of issues I have had with it.

This is a basic wireless mouse, suitable for surfing the web, working on documents or similar tasks. It’s not particularly good for gaming as it is not designed for such. If the goal is to have something that will allow you to casually use the computer for basic tasks, this one will serve. If you need a heavy-duty mouse for frequent use or you need a gaming mouse, spend a little more and get a more solid mouse.

One of the issues I have with mice is that I have huge hands and finding a mouse that fits my hand properly is a challenge. This is a smaller than average mouse, so it really doesn’t work for me. That’s not a big deal; it was designed for the large majority of people with smaller hands, so I can’t criticize this mouse for its size. It’s in that weird in-between size - smaller than the average desktop mouse but larger than a travel mouse.

The real issue I have seen with this mouse, though, is with the DPI setting. After idling for a little while, the mouse has a very nasty and predictable habit of resetting the DPI mode automatically. This is the only mouse I have used that has exhibited the problem. This impacts me when I am doing photo editing or using a graphics program and I need fine control. Sure, I can hit the DPI setting and get it to where I need it to be easily enough, but I should not have to do this over and over, particularly when I need the same setting all the time.

Other than the DPI setting, this mouse works exactly as expected. It is a decent mouse if you do not need predictable DPI settings. If you need a mouse that retains your settings, or if you need a larger mouse, or if you need a heavy-duty device, this is not the right choice for you. It’s fine for travel or casual use.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Ergonomic Wireless PC Mouse - DPI adjustable - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Sony Cyber-shot DSC-H55 14.1MP Digital Camera with 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom with SteadyShot Image Stabilization and 3.0 inch LCD (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Sony Cyber-shot DSC -H 55.
I have owned two other cameras in the past. My last Camera, before this one, was a 12 Megapixel. And I thought it, at first to be ALL THAT. This was only because my previous camera had been a four Megapixel. I was so impressed with the increase in the resolution that is all I could see was the ability to crop photos to a better end then I had been able to. After the newness had worn off I began to realize the Cameron was just a lemon. So with this camera, that mistake will not happen again. The (14 Megapixel) of this Sony camera is not that different from my (12 Megapixel) camera that I am replacing. So I will look past the resolution difference with ease.
However the (10 x) zoom lens is NEW. Not only to me, but to all (point and shoot) cameras I have ever seen. Now, the 10 x zoom lens that I am talking about is NOT digital zoom. But rather, purely optical. There is a digital zoom offered in the menus of this camera. But I simply turned this feature off. If I want to do any digital zoom, I'll do it in Photoshop on my own time.
Other perks include; a battery and charger. The battery is lithium. And knowing that a lithium battery must be conditioned before its true capacity can ever be obtained. And even before the battery had been `conditioned' it was still able to take approximately 400 shots. And of course four or five HRS of me playing around in the menus with the features. And I know from past experience this can be one of the biggest power drains on a camera battery. And this is only the first cycle. I don't foresee a need in my future to buy a spear battery.
While I am on the subject of batteries, I need to mention. The battery charger is a cute little thing. The part of the plug that actually goes into the wall will fold into the plastic housing. So it is not a burdensome piece of machinery to store. And the whole thing is extremely small. It is only 3"x2"x1". To me that sounds ridiculously small, and if it were not right here in front of me I might not even believe. But it is true. It will fit in my small camera case, instead of the drawer. I already have enough mess around my room.
Also about batteries, there is a handy little gauge, on the LCD screen, that reports the amount of battery left by a four bar indicator (like a cell phone).
I spoke earlier about the massive zoom lens. But I didn't even tell how this camera can also take a macro picture up to about 8" away at full wide angle (zoom out). The 8" I just spoke could be off a little by + or - an inch. The manual that could tell me for sure is over there in that box, and I am over here. And I'm a lazy person.
I'm really impressed at how small this camera is. It will fit very nicely, with lots of room to spare, in my chest pocket. I do wear a 2X shirt, but there is so much room left over, I bet you could fit this camera in a large size pocket. I haven't had a chance to test it; I'm just using my best estimate. On outings, being able to tuck this camera away in my pocket will be way awesome. And it is so light weight.
And it weighs very, very little for such a nice camera. I have a cordless optical mouse hooked up to this computer. So by comparing weight, the mouse is the more heavy of the two.
I think I have touched on the biggest topics I can think of at this sitting, but to sum this up. This is the best camera I (personally) have ever owned. This would include 2 other digital cameras (one SLR type & one point and shoot) and a couple `film cameras' 110 and a 35mm SLR my uncle left to me. And after comparing it with all the other ones available at the stores, it IS the best. I compare every time a store has a display, to see if mine is still better. Even some of the `better' SLR types that sell for $100's, fall short. I would be really upset to see that a little `point & shoot' can beat my $800 `SLR type' camera.
At $225 and $25 3 year extended warranty from Samsclub, I have a new gizmo and I did not break the bank.
text_fidelity_b: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-H55 14.1MP Digital Camera with 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom with SteadyShot Image Stabilization and 3.0 inch LCD (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra VOX Corded Stereo Headphones I confess, I'm not one for listening to things on earphones. I'm not attached to my iPod (I don't even have one). I don't listen to music on the bus or during lunch or anything like that. I have music on my smartphone, but I usually either plug it into the radio in my car via a cassette adapter and listen to it over the car speakers, or plug it into a speaker we got as a Christmas gift that is for use on music players/smartphones. So I all I had was a coupla dollar set of earphones from Micro Center when I absolutely had to use earphones. They were cheap and comfortable. Really, how much better can a high-priced couple of wires and earpieces be?

Mea culpa. I just did a head-for-head comparison of my cheap little blue earphones against these Jabra units. Wow. With my old earphones I could hear the fan and the television running in the background, and the sound was a bit smothered. When I changed to the Jabra VOX earphones I was awed. They were even more comfortable. The sound from the fan was completely inaudible and I could just, just tell that the television was on behind me, so I'm not saying they're noise canceling, but they do HELP reduce noise. The sound was excellent! The "smothered" sound was non-existent and the bass was especially good (I was listening to a podcast and the host has a nice deep voice). When I switched to music, the sound was much richer and I could hear a wider range of sound, and, again, the bass was excellent.

Plus the earphones come with a free app you can download that organizes your music. You can set playlists, view album covers, and it even has an equalizer.

If good sound is your goal while listening to your music device/smartphone, this is an excellent choice. My old blue earphones are going into the emergency bin as of now!
text_fidelity_b: Jabra VOX Corded Stereo Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker with aptX/AAC (Black) I am an audiophile but I always take into account the nature of the product that I am looking at or listening to. One cannot possibly expect a $99 portable bluetooth speaker to have legitimate audiophile sound. In this case, we're talking about the Creative Sound Blaster Roar. And that assertion is not in any way a knock on this product. I bought one a few days ago and I like it and am quite happy with the purchase for a variety of reasons. The main reason I like it is because the sound it produces is GOOD. That sound is not great nor is it bad. Perhaps the worst credible thing you might say about the sound is simply that it is FINE. When I consider the size of the unit (and the size of the very small speakers it contains) and the cost, I judge the sound to be GOOD. You are not going to get Martin Logan or Definitive Technology sound out of the Roar, plain and simple. Nor will you get super sound out of any of the other competitive products such as the Bose or JBL, etc. I think they all produce generally good sound for the money. The best and smartest thing a buyer can do is perhaps go to
Best Buy or any of the other retailers who carry such units and give them all a listen and look at the features they offer and then buy the one that meets your needs in terms of both sound quality and features. Having said that, for me the Roar has more features than any of the
competing units. That is simply fact and not opinion. Most of the products that are in this category seem to be made well but in my opinion, the Roar seems to be made just a little sturdier. I haven't tested that notion by dropping my Roar on the floor but in my hands it simply feels
more robust. Back to the sound question.....since I seriously doubt that many users of portable bluetooth speakers plan on doing serious
listening that entails sitting in a quite room and doing nothing but listening intently to these little portable speakers, consider how they will actually be used. Most people are playing them as background music while they are doing other things such as sitting on the beach or
cooking on the grill or in the kitchen, etc. Critical listening ain't happening here. So let's not talk about sound imaging or speaker spatiality etc. That said, for me, I don't like speakers that have a bass response that overwhelms everything else. I want a more natural sound, One that is

more balanced to my ear. Because of that, I will gravitate towards something like the Roar. If you are one who wants more bass, then you will assuredly better like the sound of any Bose product as they have made a fortune producing bass heavy products for the last 50 years. Again, for me, the features are a big deal and the Roar excels inn that regard. I won't waste your time talking about them as you can look such things up just as easily. And price is a big deal to me. The Roar 1 can be had for $99 now.... so I bought one. The Bose is $299 the last time I checked,...three times the cost of the Roar. So simply put, I loved the price of the Roar, the feature list is unmatched, it feels like military grade construction and lastly, I thought the sound was GOOD. That's why I bought it.
text_fidelity_b: Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker with aptX/AAC (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Schlage WCE100 Home Indoor Camera with Nexia Home Intelligence, White This is the best overview of the components I've seen so far:

Nexia Home Bridge (this is the key component)
Schlage touch screen deadbolt w alarm
Schlage home keypad lock
Schlage home dimmer/appliance module
Schlage home indoor camera
Schlage home outdoor camera
Trane home energy management thermostat
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) remote thermostat
Trane ComfortLink ((tm)) II Control
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) Platinum ZV control (?)
Schlage home door/window sensor
Schlage home motion sensor
Other Z-Wave sensor
Other Z-Wave thermostat
Other Z-Wave lighting device
Other Z-Wave wall switch and outlet

They might have considered making the 9V battery compartment in the "Bridge" just a little bit bigger. It's a mighty snug fit and you have to remove the battery to get the MAC ID. In fact, you have to remove the 9V battery so often it's a curiosity why the battery door is such a pain to remove and why the battery is so difficult to get out of its little bay. I was actually using a flat screwdriver to pry the battery out, it's that tight.

---

Overall, now that the camera, light dimmer and lock and installed, "enrolled" and apparently functional..? WHAT A GREAT SYSTEM!!! The components look great, they're top-quality. Now that I see everything in action (especially video of my home on my iPhone) the subscription fee seems like not such a high price to pay for what you're getting. I know that I'm going to be sorely tempted to add more cameras.

The deadbolt operates with a passcode OR with a physical key. At first I was thinking that you could lock yourself out accidentally but after examining the lock and playing with the buttons I see that is not the case.

I also understand why the light dimmer module goes so well with the indoor camera -- when it gets dark, you'd want to be able to ramp up the light enough for the camera to see! It's a temptation to put the indoor camera in one of my kids room, which is what I might have done when they were small. That would be a rude intrusion these days. So it's outside a hallway that all traffic must pass through. The field of vision nearly covers the two main doors into and out of our home, also. So I can keep an eye on who's getting home when and all that parent-of-teenagers type stuff.

Is there a controller for exterior lights? Or some kind of interface that would allow me to remotely control wired exterior lights?

The only downside to this system, aside from the kludge-y installation process, is that you will want to add more components, and they aren't cheap.

Bottom line: top-quality components, frustrating "enrollment" process -- once you get it all up and running, it's quite impressive. It's nearly worth the frustration to see it all in operation. It would be nice if you could pan-and-zoom the camera. Perhaps that will be forthcoming in another camera model.

I can't help but feel that the process of "enrolling" the components couldn't be made more simple or more streamlined.

Now to budget for an exterior camera... maybe two...

---

Now that I've seen the system in operation I grasp what the manufacturer is actually offering -- remote control of your home administered via your iPhone or iPad. Ideal for working professionals. Getting everything connected and communicating was a little effort, but it's really a beautiful system in operation. You will definitely want to add more light controls and cameras, at least I would. I wonder if there's an exterior light module? There must be. Once you see it in operation the subscription will not be an issue. You are getting more than what you're paying for.

An excellent upgrade to your home and a clever way to keep tabs on a vacation home.
text_fidelity_b: Schlage WCE100 Home Indoor Camera with Nexia Home Intelligence, White

FLAGTOP 7 in 1 USB C Hub for Universal Devices, Support 4K HDMI/PD 3.0 / USB 3.0 / 2USB 2.0 / SD/Micro SD/TF, USB Type C Dongle Hub (02A) I have a 2017 MacBook Pro with 4 Thunderbolt/USB C ports. Of course almost every peripheral I use is USB 2.0/3.0, so I have adapters everywhere and can never find one when I need it, or don’t have enough ports to plug in everything I want to use.

So this USB C Hub from Flagtop is super handy to have around. I use it to connect a second monitor (HDMI port), an external mouse/keyboard (USB 2.0 ports), and the power cable (USB C port).

I like that the USB 2.0/USB 3.0 ports have a little space between each one. This makes them usable even if you have a thick thumb drive or cable plugged in.

I had to have the ports on my laptop replaced because they loosened up over time, so I like that I can reduce wear on the new ports by unplugging the hub to disconnect everything.

The port runs warm. It’s hot to the touch; my desk feels warm underneath it.

I do wish the cable for the hub was longer. If I have my laptop on a stand, the hub dangles from one of the ports. The cable is about 5.5 inches, and if I have several things plugged into it, I feel like that’s a lot of weight to have hanging off a single port on the side of my laptop.

text_fidelity_a:
Pentax K100D Super 6.1MP Digital SLR Camera Shake Reduction and 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Lens First of all, I would like to start with highly recommending this camera to ANYONE who wants premium image quality with expandability, power and flexibility.

Pentax is one of the only companies out there that is driven entirely by photography and NOT by a marketing department that makes outrageous claims. To this end, even this, their lowest-end camera, is PACKED with premium features. Let's take a look at them:

1. Dust Reduction: Dust WILL get into your camera! This keeps it off of the sensor and increases the time inbetween cleanings.

2. Shake Reduction: It's good for a couple of stops of shooting leeway and you get it with every lens you use. Other companies build their systems into the lenses, meaning ONE lens can cost as much or more than the camera, itself! Lens-based anti-shake systems are more effective at long zoom than body-based systems, but unless you're rich, you won't be able to afford a suite of good lenses! With this camera, you can use ANY Pentax lens and get anti-shake.

3. AA batteries: Proprietary battery packs are NO GOOD. Hmmm, if you're on a shoot and your pack dies, you're not taking ANY photos unless you get a spare, right? With this camera, pick up some 2500mAh Ni-MH AA's and you can afford to get three sets. However, the power drain is so small, you might not need more than one set.

4. 6 MP sensor: Don't EVER get trapped in the megapixel hype. Megapixels mean nothing in the DSLR game, except for noise issues. Let me explain. The sensor sizes on almost all DSLRs (except for $5000 full-frame pro cameras) are APS-sized, meaning the sensor size on this camera and the Nikon D300 are very nearly the same dimensions. This means that photosensors on the chip have to be made smaller to get more pixels...meaning that the closer together/smaller sites are LESS light sensitive and they will also interfere with each other. 6 MP is a perfect sweet spot for noise and image sharpness. You get a base ISO of 200, meaning your camera is TWICE as sensitive to light as one with a base ISO of 100! This camera records color accurately and makes prints up to 8.5"x11" with no problem.

This camera has huge features and, even with the release of the K20D and K200D cameras, still maintains a good feature/image quality set with a proven CCD sensor and a suite of easy-to-learn features and settings. GE Amplified HD TV Antenna, LED Signal Strength Meter, Long Range, Supports 4K 1080P UHF VHF HDTV Channels, Amplifier Signal Booster, 10ft Coax Cable and AC Adapter, Indoor, 40529 This GE 40529 ULTRAPRO SIGNAL FINDER HD TV ANTENNA (LED Signal Meter Technology; Built in Amplifier; Indoor 60 Mile Range; VHF | UHF | HDTV; 10ft. Coaxial Cable) isn’t cheap, but it’s an excellent antenna. On my older 40” Samsung Smart TV, the antenna recognizes 48 free HDTV broadcast stations (many are local advertising channels, of course) when set up in my downstairs living room. Most of the broadcast channels display clear, non-pixelated pictures.

This is better performance than my previous favorite antenna (not amplified) which brought in about 43 stations with many pixelated displays, when set up in an upstairs bedroom with an old 26” digital/analog TV. Because I live in a hilly area, upstairs is a far, far better location for any indoor antenna in my condo. I was surprised that this antenna gets the San Jose NBC channel that is 51 miles away across many hills--the other antenna didn’t pick up that channel at all.

The signal meter, which shows 1-3 (top-row) LED lights to indicate weak, good, or strong signals for each channel, is very useful for finding the best position and orientation of the antenna in a room. I love the fact that this antenna can be mounted on a wall, can sit upright on a table (using the included stand), or can lie flat on a table.

The coaxial cable has a good, threaded connector that attaches the plug firmly to the TV antenna connector.
text_fidelity_b: GE Amplified HD TV Antenna, LED Signal Strength Meter, Long Range, Supports 4K 1080P UHF VHF HDTV Channels, Amplifier Signal Booster, 10ft Coax Cable and AC Adapter, Indoor, 40529

About the same reception (live down in a valley in a small town 40 miles from the stations)--picked up two stations, BUT had to be in the window facing the city which limits the use. We were hoping for something that picked up a little more broadly but this actually seems to be the opposite. It  has a signal booster built in, but we found no improvement. It picked up the two stations we got before with rabbit ears plus the signal cut out every 10 to 15 minutes for at least a couple second. Too bad.

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys WAP300N IEEE 802.11n 300 Mbps Wireless Access Point but can make 6 year old router work like the 6-Million Dollar man "Better, Faster, Stronger". We have a resilient [[ASIN:B00007KDVI Linksys WRT54G Wireless-G Router]] made in 2008. The only thing not great is the top speed was cutting edge 6 years ago at 54mps. Linking our older router to this Dual Band gives it a top speed of 300mps - sweet! FYI - I am totally not a techie but the setup could not have been simpler, quicker or easier.

Lynksys has a short overview video on YouTube "Linksys WAP300N Wireless Access Point" that I found helpful when needing to decide if I should order it.

Minimum System Requirements:
Access Point Mode: Existing a/b/g/n wireless router or access point
Access Point Client Mode: Existing a/b/g/n wireless router or access point + active Ethernet port on device to be connected
Wireless Bridge Mode: Additional WAP300N unit for each network connection
Wireless Range Extender Mode: Existing a/b/g/n wireless router or access point
For all operation modes: Web Browser: Internet Explorer 8, Safari 5 (for Mac), Chrome or Firefox 8 or higher for optimal browser-based configuration
PC: Wi-Fi enabled PC with CD or DVD drive, running Windows XP SP3, Windows Vista SP1 or later, Windows 7 or Windows 8
Mac: Wi-Fi enabled Mac with CD or DVD drive, running Snow Leopard 10.6.1 or later, Lion 10.7 or later, or Mountain Lion 10.8 or later
text_fidelity_b: Linksys WAP300N IEEE 802.11n 300 Mbps Wireless Access Point

[2 Pack] Firsticks Remote Case with Holder Cover for AirTag and Tile Sticker 2020 (Glow in The Dark) Compatible with Fir TV 4K,Tracker Cover for Airtag-firstick I bought this because I thought that after charging it would glow visibly in the dark, which makes it easier to find, but it does not glow. The first day I used it, it had a subtle even glow, after that, no matter how long I exposed it to the light, it only (barely) glowed unevenly on one side and not on the other. Seriously, the glow-in-the-dark star stickers I had in the '80s glowed brighter and longer than this.
On the positive side, I do like the shape and the texture, and the cover is easy to install. I do wish the material were slightly thinner on the front, so the buttons are above and not below the level of the cover, but you get used to it quickly, so no biggie. It does have a design flaw where it holds the air tag, the material there is very thick and has no openings, so the sound of the air tag is too faint, almost 20 decibels lower than without the cover, you won't be able to hear it if it fell under the furniture or under the bedsheets/blanket. In any case, the 3-star is mostly due to the fact that it does not glow; otherwise, it's not a bad product.

USB C Hub Mini Dock, Wavlink USB C Adapter with 4K HDMI, VGA, Ethernet, 2 USB 3.0 Ports,SD Card Reader with 65W PD3.0 Charging for iPad Pro/MacBook Pro 2016+/MacBook Air 2018+ and Type C Devices The physical perks of a MacBook Air are its thin, light and streamlined design- yet, thin and light has disadvantages when it comes to the built in ports usually found on the side of a laptop! After some investigating.. we found purchasing an aftermarket dock could suffice and offer those extra needs..

Wavlink’s mini dock has stepped up and provided the expected conveniences! For those who do not know- this is helpful with many extra such as: connection to printer, reading SD and mini SD card, 2 USB ports for varied items- iphone charge, light, fan etc.. Dock also allows connection to a smart TV as well- just to name options we’ve used so far!

Device has a short 6” built in cord that one plugs into the port on left side of the MacBook Air (2019) leaving just enough slack to stably set dock next to laptop on the desk and use for options as needed..

Made of lightweight aluminum material- it feels solid with no loose pieces rattling inside. Once inserted connection feels snug.. we’ve had zero issues, failures or glitches while using. Smaller in size, this can slide into backpack, briefcase etc. (truly it’s the size of a snickers candy bar! see photo included.) Feeling confident in the structure, I do suggest a protective sleeve, pouch, zip case to ensure its safety.. Something to keep it from getting dropped, lost or crushed when in transit- This is one thing I find missing that could have been included with purchase.

A docking device is a solid way to get the most from ones laptop- Without.. one wouldn't have access to all the extra features let alone, all the extra conveniences - this is a great option to fill that docking need. Hoping this info can help in your decision.. stay safe!

text_fidelity_a: Telescopes for Adults Kids Beginners, 400/70 Astronomical AZ Telescope with The Sturdy Stainless Tripod, Professional Refractor Telescope for Planetary and Terrestrial Landscape Observation. This was my first telescope.  I have read a lot about telescopes and plan on buying a much more expensive one but then I read that you can take a scope like this and upgrade the eye piece and the finder scope and have something very usable for a basic telescope.  It is below zero here so rather than go outside I did all my reviewing inside looking out my window at the mountain.  The listing provides a great overview of what you get with the scope so I won't detail it here.  I will say that it does comes with everything you need to get ab great intro into having a telescope of this type.  The trip is very shaky  and when you look out at such a great distance any movement of the tripod makes focusing difficult. Using a remote for your camera or phone would work best.  It comes with a phone adapter so I attached an older phone to it and took a couple of nice shots of a portion of the top of the mountain.  Given I didn't have to do much I thought they turned out pretty good.  The focus needs improvement but I guess I wasn't expecting a lot from this lens.  The finder scope is used to first find the object you want to see in the telescope.  It worked fine.  Then you go to the telescope lens and the object should be there and all you need to do is focus, which I did.  Because the tripod is shaky it is hard to get a good focus as just touching the eye piece cause it to shake.  This is a very inexpensive tripod and most good scopes would require a tripod 3 times the cost of this entire product.  For this price you are getting an intro to using a telescope.  With some experience with this I should be able to get better at focusing.  I took these mountain pix with the 25mm eye piece.  It comes with a nice carrying case for the scope and tripod.  There is also a nice small case for the lenses.  The instructions and well done with a nice bird watching book included also.  I will enjoy taking this with me when I go camping where maybe I will see some birds.  I highly recommend this scope as a good start for getting into this hobby.
text_fidelity_b: Telescopes for Adults Kids Beginners, 400/70 Astronomical AZ Telescope with The Sturdy Stainless Tripod, Professional Refractor Telescope for Planetary and Terrestrial Landscape Observation.

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundTrue around-ear wired headphones II - Apple devices, Navy Blue When I shop for headphones, I shop primarily for comfort. I’m not a sound snob -- I just need headphones that are super comfortable.

I’ve had a few pairs of over-ear/around-ear headphones. If I wear them too long, they give me a headache, either because they are too heavy after a while or squeeze too much or both. My last was a pair of Skullcandy’s, Hesh style, and I couldn’t wear them for more than 2-3 hours. These Bose SoundTrue’s feel a little lighter, and the ear cups are oval, not round, which makes them fit me better. They also don’t feel as tight on my head as the Skullcandy’s, but I don’t feel like they’re going to fall off.

Soundwise, I think they’re fine. But as I said, I’m not a sound snob, so as long as music sounds good and not like it’s played through a tin can, I’m happy.

Convenience wise, the ear cups swivel so the headphones fit in the included flat case. They don’t fold up a lot, but the case will be handy for when I want to take the headphones out with me. The cord is detachable, and has a remote for music/phone call control. I received the Apple version to review, so only the play/pause worked on my phone, but the other functions worked on my Macbook Air.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTrue around-ear wired headphones II - Apple devices, Navy Blue

I didn't know how bad that would suck, however. The keys are hard to read during the day. So you have no choice but to crank the backlight to max, wasting battery. Battery life is bad enough as it is. And the backlighting doesn't help much during the day. I just hate it.

Next issue is that it doesn't come with DVD playing software. Seriously? Why did I buy a computer with a DVD player in it? Asus support informs me that I should buy a third party DVD playing app as Microsoft won't let them include it. Really. I ended up researching and finding VLC player but come on. My Toshiba windows 10 laptop came with DVD playing software and it doesn't even HAVE a dvd drive!

Finally, I'm very used to having the function keys be utility keys. Brightness, volume, etc. And I like it that way. I don't use the F functions often (F11 is about the only one) and prefer to use the fn key for them when I do. Asus is set up to do the opposite. Most other manufacturers give you a way to reverse that behavior. EIther a fn lock key or a bios setting or something. Not Asus. Nope, you're stuck with it the way they like it.

Unfortunately I'm stuck with this laptop since Amazon has a lousy return policy on computers. Maybe some 13 year old will think it's cool and want to buy it. I hope so.

Kingston 64GB DataTraveler Elite G2 Black Metal Casing Fast 180MB/s R, 70MB/W USB 3.1 Flash Drive with LED light indicator (DTEG2/64GB) This is an unremarkable USB drive, with unexciting performance, for an unattractive price. (That's pretty much it for the substance of the review.)

I do my tests on a pretty fast computer with tons of memory, and an SSD system drive, while I'm doing nothing else on the computer, so no system resource constraints should affect the results. I test writes from SSD to USB, and reads in the other direction. I also use a set of 2GB test files, so that I get true results (small files can give misleading results).

I saw writes to the USB drive going between 4.5 and 8 MB/s, which is really pretty slow. I can get 16+ consistently on a little Lexar 32GB drive I have lying around. And a quick look in Amazon shows that I can find much faster USB3 drives for a bit less or a bit more, promising about 5x the write performance.

Finally, the form factor is terrible. This is a big fat ugly drive, you can get higher capacity and much better performance in slim little drives, including nano-drive size products.

Bottom line, it's ok, but I can't recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Kingston 64GB DataTraveler Elite G2 Black Metal Casing Fast 180MB/s R, 70MB/W USB 3.1 Flash Drive with LED light indicator (DTEG2/64GB)

The ideal user is someone who wants a simple to use digital camera that has the ability to instantly print the photo without dealing with a PC or conventional printer. The camera itself feels very solid, but lacks a key digital camera feature: a view screen. At first glance may seem to be a major omission. But, this camera is designed to be a high-tech replacement for the old-style Polaroid instant cameras by instantly (well, relatively instantly) printing the photo on Zink paper. Note that the paper needs to be purchased separately, and is pretty much an essential component for using the camera. While you can store photos on an SD card, the camera is really designed to be used with the Zink paper.

Usage is very straightforward – it’s about as point and shoot as you can get. That’s great for those who don’t want to fiddle with any settings, but it does put some constraints on image quality. I’ve had about 20% of my photos so far turn out less than ideal due to improper focus, poor white balance, poor resolution and/or incorrect color registration. That’s my major complaint with this camera – the paper is costly, and when you have to toss (or at least not really like) one in five photos, the cost can add up.

The images are small – the paper is only 2 by 3 inches. On the plus side it has a peel and stick backing, so you can use the photos as “post-its” very easily. Again, this is keeping with the intent of the camera, so I won’t downgrade the rating due to the small photo size.

Other negatives for me is that the battery is not user-replaceable. I’ve had too many electronic products with built-in batteries that had to be trashed since the internal battery no longer held a charge. I’m also not fond of the lens cap. It’s very easy to take off (it’s held in place by magnets) but there’s no attachment to the camera, so it’s very easy to misplace.

But this does score well with regard to ease of use and fun. As a test of ease of use I handed this to my Mom who is technically challenged, to say the least. She had no problems snapping photos and loved having the image print right there. She’s never liked using a digital camera in the past due to difficulty using it and dealing with image files. This was right up her ally.

While I’ll drop the rating to 4 stars due to the image quality issues that can crop up, overall this is a unique camera. It’s not right for everyone, but if you’re looking to revisit the days of the Polaroid instant camera while staying in the digital world, this is well worth considering.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Zink Polaroid Snap Instant Digital Camera (Pink) with ZINK Zero Ink Printing Technology

One day it just stopped charging. I had read dozens of books on there, and had the wifi plus 3g version which was very convenient.

I occasionally read now on the Kindle app on my computer, as I have about 97 books in my library, with probably 15-20 still unread. I noticed on Amazon that there was a promotion...Kindles on sale for Prime members. I thought, you know, it would be nice to read those books I've put off reading because it's just not the same on my computer or phone...I think I'll get another Kindle. I researched reviews for a little while, and decided all I needed was the Paperwhite with Wi-fi. The additional cost for 3G was just not worth it to me...sure, I'd used it before when traveling with my old Kindle to buy a few books, but with a little planning I could've purchased and downloaded the books beforehand. Also, some of the reviews of the higher end Kindles did not impress me.

Anyway, I received the Kindle earlier today. It came almost fully charged, and was so easy to set up. And within minutes had books from my Kindle library loaded! I've been reading for 2 hours straight and so far I love it. I am using it on maximum brightness, sure it may take more frequent charging, but I really love how bright it is and the contrast of the words on the page. I also bought a cover for it and find it is easier to hold IMO. Pages turned with a simple finger swipe.

Hopefully this will last a very long time! I've got so many books I want to read!

text_fidelity_a:
Aftershokz AS450 Sportz M3 Mobile Bone Conduction Headphones with Microphone (Black) purchased for single sided hearing loss after extensive research for "the best" on the market (at this or near this price point).
perks:
i can hear more clearly out of that ear using this headset. (music, netflix dialogue). if you're not deaf in one ear, this is irrelevant.
Can listen while charging, so no "down time" like some other products.
cons:
headset is uncomfortable in multiple positions. i can not really find a good position, but the least uncomfortable- and interestingly enough, the best sound quality is NOT in manufacture explained position: it's over my head with the pods near my temples or behind my ears.
Sound quality is not good, it's better coming through tinny computer speakers, but using those, i can only hear it well on my good ear. It's louder/better/and more clear (can hear fine details in the music) if you wear a headband or tight hat to press the pods against your head- but again comfort is a factor.
Noise leak is a major factor. If you turn it up to "low-normal" listening volume (cell phone set at half volume, headset set to lowest selectable volume) my housemate can still hear music played at arms reach. do not anticipate that you can wear it around others in a quiet room.

would i buy again? no.
Did I return them due to problems as stated above. Yeah.
text_fidelity_b: Aftershokz AS450 Sportz M3 Mobile Bone Conduction Headphones with Microphone (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer** There's a lot of reviews already about this product. I wavered for a good while about deciding if I wanted to accept this Cloudbook for review and now kind of wish I hadn't. As far as I'm concerned, the Cloudbook is like a merging of a laptop and a chromebook with neither giving the features that are special to each one. As far as it being a computer, it runs on Windows 10 of which I have great suspicions and doubts. If you remember, I believe most everyone received an offer for a free download of Windows 10 as an upgrade from whatever Windows program they were currently using. I have read from several sources that it was offered only as a way of installing NSA spyware on your computer. We are being watched and monitored at every turn. If you don't believe me, next time you are driving take a look at all the cameras on poles along the roads and highways and tell me we aren't being surveilled. Smartphones, smart TV's, smart refrigerators, dryers and washing machines are simply ways of letting TPTB know what we are doing at all times. How many loads of clothes you washed, what you are doing in your bedroom and on and on. So, what does all this have to do with this little and cute computer? It has Windows 10 installed.

If you are o.k. with that then overall it's not a bad machine. I really miss having a disk drive to load my own personal programs and don't like having to download stuff from the internet via the app store or some other internet source. And since it is a computer but has very little space for storage, you have to have an anti-virus program. It comes with one but it's only good for 30 days and you have to purchase it or get another one. Most of your stuff will be stored in the Cloud (like a chromebook) unless you opt for a Sandisk or external hard drive. And if you buy an external hard drive for more storage why not get a regular computer instead that has more bells and whistles and possibly a disk drive?

It looks like a chromebook and I have had to put a label on it to distinguish it from mine and my kids chromebooks. I'm having a hard time getting used to Windows 10 and it takes a long time to finally get on the internet. I have taped a piece of paper over the camera lens staring me in the face - call me paranoid if you wish but I don't like people in my house uninvited. The "shift" key is way too small and I'm always missing it.

As far as specs go they're listed on the main page but here they are again for your convenience:

11.6" HD Widescreen ComfyView LED-backlit Display (1366 x 768 resolution, 16:9 aspect ratio).
Intel Celeron N3050 Dual-Core Processor 1.6GHz with Intel Burst Technology up to 2.16GHz.
Windows 10
Intel HD Graphics
2GB of DDR3L Onboard Memory.
32GB Internal Storage
Secure Digital (SD) card reader.
802.11ac WiFi (Dual-Band 2.4GHz and 5GHz).
Bluetooth 4.0
Webcam (640 x 480)
High-definition audio support.
Two Built-in Stereo Speakers.
1 - USB 3.0 port
1 - USB 2.0 port
1 - HDMI Port with HDCP support.
Microsoft Office 365 Personal 1-Year Subscription (activation code included).
2-cell Li-polymer battery pack (4200mAh).
Up to 8 hours of battery life (Video Playback).
2.54 lbs. | 1.15kg (system unit only).

If you are already using Windows 10 then it should be easy to navigate, but I feel as if I'm learning a whole new OS though I use Windows 8 on my other laptop. It only detected two of my Bluetooth devices and I have several. If you want Word processing you must redeem your card number inside the box before a certain date or else it expires. And it's all cloud based so your data is out there and not in your pc safe and sound.

I will modify this review as needed, but I have not used this computer since a few days ago and probably will not be using it much at all. I like my chromebook better for web surfing, and it doesn't require an anti-virus program because it's totally cloud based but I never use the cloud. I store the stuff I want on my old desktop or other laptop. And my chromebook has access to a word processing program without having to buy it.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Headphones, Anbes Wireless Earbuds, IPX7 Waterproof Sports Earphones with Ear Hooks & Mic, HD Stereo in-Ear Headphones Gym Running Workout, 8 Hours Battery Noise Canceling Headsets When I first got these, I had a problem with the left earpiece not having sound, and the sound that came from the right ear was very tinny. Customer service was absolutely wonderful to resolve this for me very quickly. Since then, the sound is great! I have really small ears and I do find them a bit too big, even with the smallest cover, which keeps me from wearing them as long as I'd like. I haven't actually tried them in wet conditions, so I can't speak to this, but they are very well made and seem like they will last a long time.
--Pros
*Even though I was worried about the earpieces not being switchable, because I am left eared, this has worked alright when I am driving. I just hang the left earpiece on my shirt and use it with my right hand to work the controls.
*Charging is very fast.
*A charge last quite a long time, especially if you only use them for calls. Even listening to music it last a long time.
*The sound is nice and loud with lots of bass for listening to music.
*Call sound quality is great, for me, and for the listening party.
*The are easy to keep up with, using the nice case that they came with. It slips right into my purse or other bag.
*Well made. Durable and made with quality materials.
---Cons
*The earpieces are too large for my ears, even with the smallest cover, and my ears start to hurt after a short time.
*The pieces that go around your ears is shaped in a way that the bottom pushes into the back of my ear, causing it to get very sore.
*They are a bit larger and heavier than I'd like them to be.
*It would be nice to have a small clip for when you are driving, so that you can clip it to your shirt, to be hands free.

Overall, these are great headphones. They need a little tweaking, especially on the earpieces to make them more comfortable on the ears, but I would still highly recommend them.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Headphones, Anbes Wireless Earbuds, IPX7 Waterproof Sports Earphones with Ear Hooks & Mic, HD Stereo in-Ear Headphones Gym Running Workout, 8 Hours Battery Noise Canceling Headsets

text_fidelity_a:
turelar Compatible Headphone Jack Dongle Adapter for Phone X 8/8plus 7/7plus I received a review copy of this receiver and put it through its paces. I am going to compare it to a receiver that I've owned since 2011 and have been thoroughly pleased with: [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492TTP Bluetooth Music Receiver]].

It's a complete solution: the box contained easy-to-follow instructions and two sets of cables: one 3.5mm male at each end and the other with a 3.5mm male splitting into two RCA males. Those are a nice touch because some speakers require one or the other. With my Belkin I had to purchase an adapter to use it with one of my powered speakers. So having a complete solution right out of the box is a plus.

The receiver looks like a wall wart that plugs directly into a wall socket. It's about two inches tall and 1.75 inches wide, so it does eat up come space. Since the speaker cable comes out the bottom of the device you are pretty much locked into plugging it into the bottom receptacle.

One feature I loved is this also has a port for USB charging that allows you to keep your phone or MP3 player fully charged while playing music.

This, of course, is based on later technology and it shows. I greatly exceeded the ten meter distance limit by taking my phone to the opposite end of my house, two rooms apart from the receiver, and still managed a clear signal. Believe me, on its best day the Belkin struggled to receive a line of sight signal within a ten meter limit. I even took my phone outside and could hear clear reception coming from my speakers inside my house.

While the instruction sheet will step you through connecting to and using this receiver I did not bother to read it. I opened the bluetooth settings on my [[ASIN:B00AB7FVCY Samsung Galaxy Note II]], scanned for new devices and when BrightPlay Home showed up in the list I tapped it to connect and started streaming music to my speaker. It took longer to unpackage the receiver than it did to start using it. It does not get any easier.

The sound quality is markedly better too. I switched back and forth between the Belkin receiver and this one - attached to the same powered speakers - and could tell the difference. Not by much, mind you, but it's discernible. I had a friend listen and she agreed.

Overall this is an excellent receiver that exceeded the recommended specs in the instruction sheet and it a breeze to use. If I had to replace this it would be with an identical receiver and that is the highest praise I can bestow.
text_fidelity_b: turelar Compatible Headphone Jack Dongle Adapter for Phone X 8/8plus 7/7plus

text_fidelity_a:
Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player Picture is nice,

The real reason I'm sending the units (I've had two) back, however, is that the player refuses to output the various high quality audio formats, including 7.1 DTS Master Audio. The digital coax cable barely works and the HDMI 2 audio output simply does not work, Admittedly I have an older receiver -- a Sony STR-DA5400ES, from 2009. But it has multiple HDMI inputs and the HDMI 2 audio output on the X800 is specifically designed to send audio to an older amp. Even Sony phone support says it should work. But it doesn't.. I spent 1 hour and 7 minutes with Sony ES support today going through every possible menu permutation on both the Amp and the UBP-X800 player. No luck The HDMI is dead. Zero output. The coax output can only send DTS EX 5.1, even though the player itself tells me it's playing DTS Master Audio 7.1.

This UBP-X800 has two HDMI outputs: one for video, one for audio. In case you don't have a 4K receiver with the ever-changing HDMI protocols, you're supposed to be able to feed HDMI audio to the amp. So I fed the video directly to the Samsung's video input (a direct cable connection) and another HDMI to my amp.

Zero audio from the player's HDMI audio feed. Not a peep of audio at all.

So I used the orange RCA digital audio coax connector to get surround sound audio.

But the coax digital audio cable only delivers DTS EX 5.1, not the 7.1 DTS Master Audio available on the Kingsman 4K disk. I updated the player's and the TV's firmware and read the manual. Nothing fixes the problem. Using all new, very short, high-speed HDMI 2.0 cables too.

My ancient Sony BDP-S560 Blu-ray player feeds all formats to the same 5400ES amp properly. I get great 7.1 DTS Master HD audio. Thus my old Blu-ray player sounds way better than my brand new advanced Sony UHD player.
Researching at the Sony forum under the UBP-X800 Audio Problems thread, answers were all over the place and none worked, I tried to register so I could post my problem and the website wouldn't allow me to. The comments there were complaining that they could not get the ATMOS tracks working.

I have no choice but to pack both X800s up and send them back.

Eventually I found that I needed to plug the 4K player into input 3 of the TV for the image to stabilize. Interesting that only some inputs on the TV can handle UHD source. But still, the player's audio doesn't work with my Sony Amp (Sony's fault).

HDMI was supposed to solve all these problems, but I suspect the HDCP copy protection schemes are really screwing things up or the firmware has bugs or companies just produce inferior products. Rather disappointing.
text_fidelity_b: Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Powershot A1200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Zoom (Silver) (OLD MODEL) OK, here are the facts: my other (similar) camera developed a glitch -- it will not allow me to delete photos without loooooong delays. So I went in search of an inexpensive replacement camera. I settled on this Canon.

I did so with trepidation because some of the reviews were lukewarm at best. Yet other reviewers loved it. (This, by the way, is what makes horse races!) So I thought I would take a chance.

Here is why I am happy with my choice: (1) the viewer seems larger than its dimensions suggest; (2) the camera fits in my shirt pocket; (3) the pics are crisp indoors and out; (4) the on-off button is clearly marked and the shot button is nice and robust. For me, these features are all I need. To be sure, the camera has a few video bells and whistles -- I'll try those one of these days. No rush.

A Con: the shot button takes a little getting used to, since it appears to have two stages to it. If you just press and disengage, nothing will happen. It requires a little patience and then it will take the picture. I can live with that idiosyncrasy.

Another Con: no internal memory. You must purchase an SD card before you can use the camera. This too I have accepted, because having pics on cards does make it easy to load them into PCs and laptops.

If you are looking for a simple "point-and-shoot" camera that will also perform other tricks if you are of a mind, go for it!
text_fidelity_b: Canon Powershot A1200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Zoom (Silver) (OLD MODEL)

Logitech for Creators Blue Yeti X Professional USB Condenser Microphone for PC, Mac,Gaming,Recording, Streaming, Podcasting on PC, Desktop Mic High-Res Metering, LED Lighting,Blue VO!CE Effects-Black This is a fancier version of the popular Blue Yeti amateur-quality USB microphone with a much higher price tag ($170 vs $110). For the extra money, you get 4 condensers (instead of 3) to give you higher-resolution 24-bit audio (instead of 16-bit) plus a bunch of fancier control and display options. The new microphone has the same directional recording patterns to isolate the recording to your intended audio sources. Is the new microphone worth the extra money? If you really need 24-bit audio, then definitely yes. If not, the new display and control features are more convenient than a huge jump in functionality. The Blue Yeti is still a great microphone for amateur USB recording (podcasts, musical performances, etc). The new version is a step forward, but not worth the price for everyone.

My biggest complaint is that the new microphone uses the same ancient mini-USB interface as the old one. Modern ultralight laptops are moving to the USB-C standard and mini-USB is 2 generations old. You could use a USB-C hub to give you a mini-USB interface, but I wish all modern devices came with USB-C ports since this has been the standard for the last few years.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech for Creators Blue Yeti X Professional USB Condenser Microphone for PC, Mac,Gaming,Recording, Streaming, Podcasting on PC, Desktop Mic High-Res Metering, LED Lighting,Blue VO!CE Effects-Black

text_fidelity_a: BT21 Baby Wireless Silent Mouse by Royche (Koya) I adore this wireless mouse! I bought it to liven up my workspace and get rid of my wired mouse. I am so happy with my purchase. I bought my mom the RJ one and she loves it too! It’s very comfortable to use and while I wouldn’t say it’s exactly silent, it is much quieter than a regular mouse. I also love that you can store the USB connector inside the mouse when traveling to avoid losing it. The only thing that could have made this mouse even better is if it scrolled right and left too, but it’s not so sever that it merits less stars. It utilizes a USB connector and is not a Bluetooth mouse. It is battery powered and comes with the battery out of the box.
text_fidelity_b: BT21 Baby Wireless Silent Mouse by Royche (Koya)

text_fidelity_a: Western Digital 2TB WD Blue SN570 NVMe Internal Solid State Drive SSD - Gen3 x4 PCIe 8Gb/s, M.2 2280, Up to 3,500 MB/s - WDS200T3B0C Our budget Lenovo (IdeaPad 3 15IIL05) came with a 256GB SSD. To make it more useful, I originally paired it with an external WD Black 500 GB hdd. That has its limitations, though, as it's not very transportable. After the warranty expired, upgrading to the 1 TB internal SSD was simple. Lots of online videos on how to remove the back cover and locate the SSD. First I took the new SSD and put it into an SSD enclosure I also purchased on Amazon. Then I was able to format it with Windows from the existing SSD (hidden partition). Finally I removed the laptop cover, took the old SSD out and put the new SSD in. The old SSD went into the SSD external enclosure. It was easy to copy all the files from the external hdd to the new 1 TB drive, and I've been up and running with no issues. No problems with portability, either (the 500GB hdd is semi-retired; I only pull it out on rare occassions). Great upgrade!
text_fidelity_b: Western Digital 2TB WD Blue SN570 NVMe Internal Solid State Drive SSD - Gen3 x4 PCIe 8Gb/s, M.2 2280, Up to 3,500 MB/s - WDS200T3B0C

text_fidelity_a:
Skullcandy Crusher Wireless Over-Ear Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone and Android with Microphone / 40 Hours Battery Life / Extra Bass Tech / Great for Music, School, Workouts, and Gaming - Grey/Tan I got these from Best Buy after reading the glowing and praising reviews, assuming these would compliment my heavily-bassed up music (which is easily more than 3/4 of what I have- I'm literally all about that bass). Honestly, they are terrible when I listen to anything pumped with bass (ie Kesha, Die Antwoord, Zedd, etc). I can't explain it, but something about the sound makes me cringe- it's so distorted and just not good.

HOWEVER, I then tried listening to other genres like rap and rock, and oh my god those songs sound FLAWLESS on these headphones. They just compliment each other so well. It's just so unusual because I thought these headphones were going to bring a whole new positive experience to... well.. bass-y music? Instead it sounds like, well, close your eyes and picture sitting in your car at a red light and hearing one of those annoying people pull up beside you who have a terrible quality radio and speakers and all you hear is distorted and muffled "BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM BOOOOM BOOOOOOOOOOOM"s. That's legit what these Skullcandys sound like and that's only when the bass booster is at MID POINT. I tried putting it all the way up to the highest setting and it sounded like pure garbage.

I'm not an audiophile, BUT I am obsessed with bass and can tell when it's good or not- and Skullcandy definitely dropped the ball on these. I would highly recommend finding another pair if your most listened to genre is heavy dance/electronic/pop/club, BUT these are breathtaking if you listen to genres or any music in general with minimal bass.

Other positives- SO comfortable (I used to have other Skullcandy Crushers and they gave me head aches), sleek (old ones were bulky and imo ugly), VERY easy to use (literally took seconds to pair and figure out), feels durable and like it's made with high quality materials, and had absolutely no connectivity issues.

Overall I'm giving this a 4/5. I'm extremely sad that I'm returning them but they just aren't for me. I hyped myself up so much only to be let down by distortion and overpowering buzzing thumping. I won't lie or give these 1 star because I'm sorry but that's just ridiculous. These headphones are wonderful, just not quite on the money.
text_fidelity_b: Skullcandy Crusher Wireless Over-Ear Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone and Android with Microphone / 40 Hours Battery Life / Extra Bass Tech / Great for Music, School, Workouts, and Gaming - Grey/Tan
